text: Color and style, driven by the data itself instead of set by hand. Three ways to do it, starting with the most common.
Rules: green above a target, yellow near it, red below. Set each range as a percent of the overall spread, or as a literal number — mixing those two up is the single most common mistake here.
Data bars turn each cell into a small bar chart — longer bar, higher value. Toggle Show bar only to let the bar speak for itself, no number needed.

Icons attach a status symbol to each value — a diamond, a triangle, a circle — readable at a glance, no legend required. And this same Gradient, Rules, and Field value logic works well beyond tables — charts, cards, and slicers all support it too.
Next: the Filters pane — every level a filter can apply at, from one visual up to the whole report.
